# The Role of AI Trust in Human-AI Collaboration Performance

## Introduction

Human-AI collaboration has become a central topic in organizational research (Bakker et al., 2023; Lee & See, 2004; Mayer et al., 1995). Scholars have long argued that trust is a critical mechanism governing cooperative behavior (Mayer et al., 1995). As artificial intelligence increasingly enters the workplace, employees must decide whether to rely on algorithmic recommendations.

Trust in automation research suggests that appropriate calibration of trust improves decision quality (Lee & See, 2004). Job demands-resources theory has also been applied to understand technostress (Bakker & Demerouti, 2017).

## Theory and Hypotheses

Following conservation of resources theory (Hobfoll, 1989), we propose that depleted resources reduce employees' capacity to verify AI outputs. Based on the trust calibration model (Lee & See, 2004), we hypothesize that appropriately calibrated trust positively relates to collaboration performance.

**H1:** AI trust is positively related to human-AI collaboration performance.

Prior field studies support this link in medical and logistics settings (Dzindolet et al., 2003; Parasuraman & Riley, 1997; Pop et al., 2015).

## Method

We conducted a two-wave survey of 312 employees using established scales (Mayer & Davis, 1999).

## Results

Results supported H1 (β = .34, p < .01).

## Discussion

Our findings extend trust research (Ferrario et al., 2020). Machine behavior research also offers useful perspectives (Rahwan et al., 2019).
